The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8445a9b1c8e5a4c3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 52-53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let d ≥ 4 and 2 ≤ n ≤ d − 2 be integers, and let µ be an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure satisfying (1.2). Fix ρ > 2 and a real odd C2 convolution kernel K satisfying (8.1). For every real f ∈ L2(µ), Vρ((TK,µ ε f)ε>0) L2(µ) ≤ C2∥f∥L2(µ). (8.3) The principal value TK,µ f(x) = lim ε↓0 TK,µ ε f(x) exists finitely for µ-almost every x, belongs to L2(µ), and ∥TK,µ ε f − TK,µ f∥L2(µ) −→ 0 (ε ↓ 0). The vector Riesz family Rµ,εf satisfies the analogous hard-variation bound and has an almost- everywhere principal-value limit, with strong convergence in L2(µ; Rd). The exceptional null set may depend on K and f. These are strong-convergence assertions on each input; no operator-norm convergence is asserted. For the fixed profile (8.2), every real f ∈ Lp(µ) with 1 < p < ∞ satisfies Vρ((TK,µ φ,ε f)ε>0) Lp(µ) ≤ Cp∥f∥Lp(µ). (8.4) 52 For every real f ∈ L1(µ) and λ > 0, µ n x : Vρ((TK,µ φ,ε f)ε>0)(x) > λ o ≤ C1 λ ∥f∥L1(µ). The constants may depend on the dimensions, the fixed ρ, the kernel bounds, the uniform-rectifiability data, and, for the smooth estimates, the chosen profile and p when relevant.
